subject: ISV co-sell credits and lead guardrails — framework proposal
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Subject: ISV co-sell credits and lead guardrails — framework proposal

Hi Claire / Mike,

Great to connect last week — thanks again for the product walkthrough. As promised, attached is a lightweight framework that captures how Redwood would approach co-sell credits, lead registration, and reseller/referral flows with Integratech. High-level highlights: 

- Revenue-share vs referral: We propose a referral credit (one-time booking credit) for introduced leads, and a separate reseller margin model for when Integratech transacts as the reseller of record.
- Tiered referral credit: 8% for ARR < $50k, 12% for $50k–$250k, 15% > $250k, applied to first-year ARR on closed renewals that originated from a registered lead.
- Lead registration window: 90-day protection window from first qualified introduction; protection is lost if lead engages directly with Redwood prior to contract signature.
- Co-sell credit stacking: credits are single-origin — we avoid double-counting when both partners introduce the same opportunity.
- Integration milestones: For any reseller commitment, a technical integration milestone (API connector + usage test) must be completed within 60 days for reseller pricing to kick in.
- Data & support: Integratech will get token-limited access to account-level telemetry for joint opportunities; Redwood provides NBD support for integration-enabled deals.

Please find attached co-sell-framework-draft-v1.pdf with more detail and example payout scenarios. Can you review and flag the must-haves vs negotiables on your side? If it helps, I can get Legal and Channel Ops on a follow-up call next week.

Proposed times: Tue 2026-06-23 09:00-10:00 PT or Wed 2026-06-24 11:00-12:00 PT.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships (Americas)
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: ISV co-sell credits and lead guardrails — framework proposal

Soojin, thanks for the draft — super helpful. Mike and I chatted and added inline redlines (attached). Quick notes from our side: 

- Lead protection: 90 days feels tight for our sales motion; can we discuss extending to 180 days for enterprise-tier leads (ARR > $250k)?
- Stacking: We need a clear priority rule if a lead is introduced by both Integratech and another partner — suggestion: first-to-register gets protection, but if both demo, split the credit 60/40.
- Reseller margins: Your draft shifts reseller economics toward fixed discounts; we prefer a margin % tied to net ARR retention for the first 12 months.
- Billing & tax: Who handles tax and invoicing when Integratech is reseller of record? We need this in the MSA appendix.

I've attached integratech-redlines.docx with comments. We're generally aligned on the integration milestone but want the 60-day window to be extendable by mutual agreement. Let's take the call — Tue 09:00 PT works for me.

—Claire

Thanks for the ping. Quick take from Channel Ops / GTM: 

1) Lead protection window: We can be flexible — 180 days for enterprise makes sense if we add a lead qualification handshake (BANT-lite) and require Integratech to register the lead in HubSpot with the originating rep cc'd. That protects our pipeline hygiene.

2) Split credit: I prefer to avoid fractional stacking except as an exception. Proposed policy: first-to-register gets full credit; if both partners can demonstrate equivalent engagement (meeting notes, signed NDA, or equivalent) within 30 days of registration, we escalate to a 60/40 split (originator 60%). This keeps things simple while handling legitimate disputes.

3) Reseller margin model: Suggest tying reseller discount to a 12-month retention SLA: 20% discount baseline, with +5pp for >90% retention and -5pp if <70% retention in year one. Billing: reseller of record handles invoicing; Redwood issues partner credit via a contra entry tied to the closed opportunity. Legal should add tax handling clause (reseller responsible for local taxes unless otherwise agreed).

4) Integration milestone: keep 60 days but allow 30-day extension on mutual written agreement. 

I'll draft suggested language for the partner play appendix and loop Legal for the tax/invoicing clause. If we agree, we can send a near-final playbook ahead of the call.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Claire / Mike — thanks for the detailed redlines and patience while we reviewed internally. Summary of where Redwood is today: 

- Lead protection: We can accept a 180-day protection window for enterprise-tier leads (ARR > $250k) provided Integratech registers the lead in HubSpot with the originating rep cc'd and provides a one-paragraph qualification note (to minimize spam).
- Split credit: We prefer first-to-register as the default. If both parties can demonstrate equivalent engagement within 30 days, we will apply a 60/40 split (originator 60%).
- Reseller margin & billing: We agree to a baseline 20% reseller discount with performance-linked adjustments (+5pp / -5pp) tied to net ARR retention in the first year. Integratech to be reseller of record; Redwood issues partner credits on close. Legal will add the tax/invoicing clause.
- Integration milestones: 60 days by default; 30-day extension by mutual written agreement.

Next steps: Marissa will send a redlined partner-play appendix (channel play + billing/tax language) by EOD tomorrow. Can we confirm the Tue 2026-06-30 09:00 PT slot for a 30-minute alignment call to finalize the playbook and decide whether we move to a pilot reseller engagement?
